themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it: generate only from pre-approved claims, and accept that a person still decides the edge cases.
themes.evidence: All three models on governing generative marketing content say contextual legal and brand meaning cannot be automated, and all three answer with a registry of approved claims tied to evidence that generation must cite; the same point recurs in the semantic context layer work, where teams hold genuinely different meanings of the same term.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or by admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On content review one model notes you can never count the mistakes review missed, on answer engine optimization the models say model drift swamps their own effect, and on identity resolution and B2B buying-group signal they say confidence numbers and intent models cannot be validated without an answer key nobody has.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three models put a proxy or gateway in front of every write with hard spend and audience caps, consent enforcement gets a single egress checkpoint, journey orchestration gets one shared pre-send check, and content governance constrains generation up front rather than checking afterwards.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, a message, or a buying conversation leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, trained model, or private chat that now holds it. You can estimate whether the rules were honored, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion the models call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes with no accepted test for removal from a trained model, incrementality work says platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and B2B intent work says early buying conversations happen in private channels that cannot be observed.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the person holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The models increasingly try to make honesty pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic all three models propose a fast lane with better data or prices for agents that declare themselves, because agents gain by pretending to be human and no one wants the liability for lying; journey orchestration stalls on channel owners paid for saying yes, and the semantic layer stalls on teams that keep definitions apart on purpose.
